correctness.rationale: Independent reconstruction from the Gram kernel gives the exact row integral. Convexity in the scalar evaluation basis value reduces all rows to endpoints. A strict support-variance identity makes both endpoint kernels have exactly one sign-changing zero; the antiderivative then proves both branch formulas for every positive rate. The small-rate derivatives follow from uniform kernel Taylor expansions at simple zeros and give ±4/27; the large-rate explicit expansions give the logarithmic boundary layer and the opposite row tending to one. The checker passed 243 supplementary tests; no finite sampling substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: Continuous exponential-mode least-squares fitting is a natural stable/unstable linear approximation operator. The norm controls worst-case bounded measurement error and the exact negative part controls positivity loss. The result gives a complete rate-dependent computable constant (not merely an upper bound), pinpoints the boundary layer at log(2lambda)/lambda, and quantifies an asymmetry: the sharp gain changes from 5/3 to nearly three despite the model space staying dimension two. This is more than an arbitrary finite example or a recomputation of the known general envelope.
